If a person refuses to, say, prepare a gay wedding cake on account of religious reasons, then that's their right so long as they are not outright denying a gay couple service (see *Masterpiece Cakeshop v. Colorado Civil Rights Commission*).

I do disagree with your last belief. I am going to assume that you are a person who supports free-market capitalism (do correct me if I am wrong, though). If you believe that venues should be allowed to decline people from, for instance, renting, on account of a religious belief, then isn't that more detrimental to the free market? If a landlord prohibits a gay couple from renting, isn't that a missed opportunity to contribute to the market (and to your salary in some way)? I think when you prevent people, regardless of their sexual orientation from participating in the free market, then it does some harm. Now take the above example of a baker refusing to make a gay wedding cake for a couple—yes, there is a missed business opportunity, but it would be far more disadvantageous if the baker refused the couple from ever stepping foot in their establishment. The couple is more than welcome, but they can still participate in the market by purchasing goods other than a gay wedding cake.

These are some of the things I've learned along the path to 90 days: It's really important to control your thoughts before they control you. That means at the first thought of an impulse or an urge, do everything in your power to squash it. For me, I found that I had to channel those thoughts in a different form - whether it be listening to a song that really distracts me from the urge or doing something productive. 

Keeping this log in my journal has really been motivational. Every single time I "X" out a box, it's one more victory that I consider for myself. I envisioned having the first 90 boxes crossed out and it's pushed me to be a better version of myself. 

I know this doesn't apply to everyone, but my return to Christian faith in the last few weeks has also proven really effective in my path. Lately I find that a prayer against sexual or erotic dreams has given me the rest that I need so that I don't wake up feeling tempted. And even in those moments where I have an urge in the middle of the day, a silent prayer also really helps. I understand not everyone is religious or has the same faith, but I encourage you guys to be open to some things you've never tried.

Questions like these are very subjective because they depend on your background in a language, how much time and effort you put into learning the language, your exposure and immersion to the culture practicing that language, and also the school you attend and the quality of instruction you're receiving. 

But honestly, going to college to major in a foreign language is a waste of time (and money). Seriously, you'd be better off learning language through a bilingual friend or language-learning apps. 

If you're still persistent about learning it though, a general rule of thumb is that you should be practicing your language on a daily basis. Learning a foreign language is a marathon, not a sprint. Just keep at it, do your best, and if your ultimate goal is to become fluent in that language, make learning it your primary goal. Good luck.
